added_failures_note: derived by the reviewer from the reviewed run's own arm logs, because its manifest carries no literal baseline_suite/after_suite field: baseline arm logs/base/combined.run{1,2}.log (239 passed each) and after arm logs/head/combined.run1.log (239 passed at 2a4f7da05+worktree) carry no FAILED/ERROR line, so the id set failing at head that passed at base is empty. The instrument is shown to see a failure: the same grep over logs/load/test_follower_checks_its_owner.run{1,2}.log returns tests/test_follower_checks_its_owner.py::test_a_read_only_follower_leaves_when_its_own_owner_dies, so the zero is a measurement rather than a blind parser. The store's read path (reckon/crew/review.py annotate_review_of_run) re-derives from the two manifest fields alone, so a reader through read_review sees this pair as unmeasured while the file on disk carries the figure above.

findings.text: OWNER_CHECK_SECONDS = 0.1 is defined but read nowhere in the file: the assertion at :773 reads only OWNER_CHECK_PASSES (20), and the comment above derives that 20 from the 0.1 s cadence in prose, so the cadence and the tolerance are decoupled and a reader who changes the poll interval must recompute the pass tolerance by hand rather than from the code.

the only red is the "still running long after" pytest.fail in _passes_until_exited (tests/test_follower_checks_its_owner.py:562), so the executed control shows the harness reddens but never exercises the reworked assertion at :773; a follower that detects the dead owner yet lingers past the tolerance — the exact case the tolerance exists to catch — is not demonstrated by the record. The declared control string on line 1 is "restore one changed id's original fixed wait or wall-clock bound", which the log's line 2 itself reports was instead run as a product mutation to reckon/cli.py (_check_consumer gated to the follower's first second), so the first line names a mutation that was not run. (I reproduced the count assertion's red path independently: a scratch cli.py mutated to linger 50 passes after the owner is gone reddens it with "the holder ran 50 and the read-only follower 50".)

the three head arms' first line names 2a4f7da0507cb081b7b233b4307218662a55c1c3+worktree rather than the revision the change landed as (e511d849), so the gate logs the done-when asks to head with the revision do not tie the measured file to a commit; the manifest asserts the run-time worktree was byte-identical to e511d849, which a reader cannot check from the logs (the mtimes place the arms at 21:34, before the 21:38:54 commit, and the negative control at 21:43 after it, so the assertion is consistent but unverifiable from the record).

the control's own module line reports the import resolving to the worktree's reckon/__init__.py while the manifest's measurement_module names /tmp/negctl2-lsihu/reckon/__init__.py; the two disagree, so the header does not establish that the mutated scratch source was the module under test, even though the red message does establish it, so the manifest asserts the datum the header contradicts rather than naming the value the run printed.

item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, two commits, one changed path, nine log groups, each named id's bound and mechanism at file and line, and an executed control — its tests field is a literal command with no placeholder, but the head-arm headers name the parent revision, the control log's module line names the worktree tree rather than the scratch tree, and OWNER_CHECK_SECONDS is defined at :103 and read nowhere.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the fence grants six test files, an evidence fragment and a figure dir; the two commits change exactly tests/test_follower_checks_its_owner.py, the reviewed worktree is clean at e511d849, and no product file, plan file, fragment, figure or peer path was touched.

justifications.durability: the assertion now reddens on the mechanism's own signal rather than on node speed: I mutated a scratch reckon/cli.py so the follower detects the dead owner but lingers 50 wait passes, and the reworked id failed with "the holder ran 50 and the read-only follower 50" against the tolerance of 20, so the count guard discriminates a follower that notices late, while the live-owner control at :773's sibling assertion still requires a follower with a live owner to survive; the pass count is load-independent (a starved pass counts as one), which is what removes the old host-speed dependency.
justifications.evidence: the run's evidence is now essentially sound — each arm log is headed revision/tree/lgrep-able command and ends EXIT=, the negative control is a single red, my independent scratch run at e511d849 reproduced 5 passed, and I re-derived the added-failure count as 0 with a positive control — but the control's red is the timeout path rather than the reworked assertion, its first line declares a mutation the run did not execute, the head-arm headers name the parent revision, and the control log's module line contradicts the manifest's measurement_module.
justifications.fit: the new helper _passes_until_exited and _pass_count sit beside _wait_until_exited and follow the file's measured-narrative idiom, the new names carry no plan, ticket or version label, and FOLLOWER_TEST_PASS_LOG is armed only for the one case so the reload cases keep the byte-identical plain launch they identify an image by — the only blemish is OWNER_CHECK_SECONDS defined at :103 and read nowhere.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the mechanism the §3 goal prefers is now used: the changed id waits on the follower's observed owner-check passes (the mechanism's own cadence) instead of a wall-clock bound, EXIT_WITHIN_SECONDS is restored to 2.0 for every other use, and the file passes 5/5 in three loaded head arms and in my own scratch run; the other five named ids are unchanged and green, which the done-when permits where their bound records a real guarantee.
justifications.scope_discipline: the two commits change tests/test_follower_checks_its_owner.py alone, one of the six files the node declared, and the reviewed worktree is clean at e511d849 with no product source, plan file or peer-owned path in the diff.
